newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares gain ground in late IBIS trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares gain ground in late IBIS trade.

text.p: German shares advanced nearly half a percent in afternoon electronic trade on Friday, supported by the ongoing rise of the dollar to above 1.86 marks and early firmness on the Dow Jones Industrial index.
At 1351 GMT, the IBIS DAX index was up 24.59 points, or 0.56 percent, at 4,430.11 points. The index fell to 4,393.30 points earlier, but support at 4,400 generally stayed intact.
"Volumes have been mostly modest today, but things are picking up as the day progresses. There were extremely high volumes in Daimler-Benz earlier on," a Frankfurt trader said.

Daimler was one of the focuses of attention in early trade, as the share fell after U.S. investment banks Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley downgraded 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates for Daimler. Merrill also cut Daimler to intermediate reduce from neutral but left the share as a long-term hold.
The downgrades came after Daimler released six-month figures that showed group operating profit more than doubling to 1.849 billion marks.
Daimler CEO Juergen Schrempp said he did not understand the disappointment among analysts, and described on Friday in a radio interview the company's performance as "excellent".
Shares in Daimler recovered slightly, but were still down 2.45 percent at 149.10 marks in late trade.
The other big corporate news of the afternoon was the announcement that German software group SAP AG were planned a hook-up with Intel to form an Internet joint venture.
SAP shares were up 1.50 marks at 449.50 marks in afternoon trade. "We are very happy with this news -- it's perfect news," a trader said.
U.S. payroll data brought the market lower initially but the market soon righted itself.
U.S. non-farm payrolls rose 316,000 in July, above the forecast, and June personal income rose 0.6 percent, also above forecast.
In late trade the IBIS DAX took a sharp downturn after Wall Street tumbled on the back of NAPM data.

For next week dealers said they were looking ahead to first-half figures from Adidas AG, Veba AG and Schering figures, as well as German unemployment data from Nuremberg on Wednesday and German industrial orders data.
